title: U.S. House · Michigan's 4th District
area: Michigan's 4th Congressional District — southwestern Michigan, including Kalamazoo and Benton Harbor.

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 4th District R+3 for the 2026 cycle. Donald Trump won the district 52.0%–46.5% in 2024.
Incumbent Bill Huizenga defeated Philip Tanis in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary. Sean McCann defeated Diop Harris II in the Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Bill Huizenga
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Michigan's 4th District (since 2023); in the U.S. House since 2011

summary.text: Huizenga is the incumbent U.S. Representative, first elected in 2010 to represent Michigan's then-2nd District and representing the current 4th District since redistricting took effect in 2023. A co-owner of a family gravel business, he worked as a realtor and as a congressional aide, and served in the Michigan House of Representatives before running for Congress. In the 119th Congress he is vice chair of the House Financial Services Committee and chairs its Foreign Affairs subcommittee on South and Central Asia.

background.text: Born January 31, 1969, in Zeeland, Michigan; according to his campaign website, he was born and raised in Ottawa County. He graduated from Holland Christian High School (1987) and earned a B.A. in political science from Calvin College (1991).

According to his House biography, he began his career as a realtor and entrepreneur; Wikipedia dates his real estate work to the early 1990s. He co-owns Huizenga Gravel Inc., a family business in Jenison, Michigan, and his campaign website describes him as a third-generation small business owner.
Worked as Director of Public Policy for then-U.S. Rep. Pete Hoekstra (R) from 1997 to 2003.
Elected to the Michigan House of Representatives (90th District, Ottawa County) in 2002 and re-elected in 2004 and 2006, after which he was term-limited.

Won the 2010 Republican primary for Michigan's 2nd District after Hoekstra left the seat to run for governor, then won the general election over Democrat Fred Johnson, 64% to 32%. He has been re-elected in each cycle since.

In the 119th Congress he is vice chair of the House Financial Services Committee, chairs the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia and sits on its Africa subcommittee. In the 118th Congress he chaired the Financial Services Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.

Since 2017 he has been elected by colleagues as a co-chair of the bipartisan Great Lakes Task Force, and he is the Republican co-chair of the Bipartisan Fiscal Forum, a group focused on the federal debt.
According to his campaign website, he lives in Ottawa County with his wife, Natalie, and their five children.

priorities.text: Says he has focused on fiscal discipline and lower costs for energy, groceries, and housing in response to inflation.
Supports expanding American energy production, saying it will lower utility bills and strengthen the economy.
As a member of the House Financial Services Committee, has worked to remove regulations he says burden small businesses' access to capital.

positions.summary: A member of the Pro-Life Caucus, has worked to prevent taxpayer funding of abortion, supported legislation such as the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act, and opposes late-term abortions.
positions.quote: As a member of the bipartisan pro-life caucus, Congressman Huizenga has remained steadfast in his defense of the unborn by working to prevent taxpayer dollars from being used to fund abortions; promote quality care centers over abortion facilities; and advocate against gruesome, late-term abortions.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves as vice chair of the House Committee on Financial Services and chairs the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia.

Introduced the Deport the Terrorists Act, which would allow the federal government to strip citizenship from, and deport, naturalized U.S. citizens convicted of financing, materially supporting, or committing acts of terrorism.

candidates.name: Sean McCann
candidates.currentRole: Michigan State Senator, District 19 (Kalamazoo area); in the state Senate since 2019

summary.text: McCann is a Michigan state senator from Kalamazoo who previously served in the Michigan House and worked in the nonprofit sector. Term-limited in the state Senate, he announced in July 2025 that he would run for Michigan's 4th District and won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary. He is the Democratic nominee against incumbent Bill Huizenga.

background.text: Born in Michigan; earned a B.A. in political science from Western Michigan University (1993).
Served as executive director of Kalamazoo Friends of Recreation, director of financial development for the American Red Cross, and executive director of the Vine Neighborhood Association.
Served in the Michigan House of Representatives (District 60) from 2011 to 2015.

Elected to the Michigan Senate in 2018 (District 20) and took office in 2019; has represented District 19, which includes Kalamazoo and surrounding municipalities, since 2023. His campaign says the district makes up about one-third of the 4th Congressional District.
In the 2025-2026 session he serves as Majority Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and chairs the Energy and Environment Committee.
Under Michigan's term limits he could not seek another Senate term. He announced his congressional campaign on July 14, 2025, and defeated Diop Harris II in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary.

record.text: In the Michigan Senate's 2025–2026 session, serves as Majority Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and chairs the Energy and Environment Committee; also sits on the Finance and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

candidates.name: Shafina Barnett

summary.text: Barnett is the Green Party nominee for Michigan's 4th District, running against Republican incumbent Bill Huizenga and Democratic nominee Sean McCann.

researchNotes: This is a competitive lean-Republican seat (R+3); research time focused on the two major-party candidates. Huizenga's official and campaign issues pages (economy, energy, budget, homeland security) discuss policy generally but do not directly address immigration enforcement, tariffs, gun laws, or taxes on high earners in terms specific enough to document a position on those ISSUES statements.
